<reason>A won a close debate by keeping the motion’s even-if structure in view and turning B’s concession that remaining primary forest and deep peat should not be converted into a timing/instrument comparison: B’s mapping-fire-buyer sequence still leaves that land legally convertible. B’s capture and scarcity-rent attacks were sharper political economy, but they did not neutralize the cheap-channel argument or convert “some smallholder opportunity cost” into a reason to vote down a motion that already prices that cost in.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s R2/closing against B’s toolkit: fire and concession law punish smoke after the fact and do not retire the permit, so sequencing without a hard stop is a land race with better manners.</best_rebuttal>
